trust_decision.summary: Command-based TACACS+ authorization decides permit/deny by matching operator-configured regexes against the client-supplied joined cmd-arg string; the regexes are applied unanchored (substring match), so a permit rule matches any argument string that merely contains the pattern.

landing_point.why: The only regexp call in the repo; 'permissive regular expression' leads straight to the regexp.MatchString in CommandBasedAuthorizer.evaluate.

fix_sites.entry_point: TACACS+ authorization request (service=shell, cmd=X) -> stringy Authorizer.Handle (cmds/server/config/authorizers/stringy/stringy.go:83) -> CommandBasedAuthorizer.evaluate
public library API tacquito.Args (new CommandArgsNoLE added next to CommandArgs; trailing cmd-arg=<cr> stripped so anchored regex still matches)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: authorize_fields.go:185-195 (Args.CommandArgs in the root tacquito package; the fix adds CommandArgsNoLE there to drop a trailing <cr> line ending)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver could say the <cr> line-ending handling in the root protocol package is a separate cosmetic concern, not part of a regex-anchoring fix, and leave CommandArgs alone. Anchoring without stripping then makes legitimate 'cmd-arg=<cr>' requests fail, so this is a must-keep-working break, not a security hole.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Devices send a trailing 'cmd-arg=<cr>'. The documented form 'cmd=show cmd-arg=system cmd-arg=<cr>' must still be permitted by an anchored rule such as 'system'. A '<cr>' in the middle must be kept, and rules the operator already anchored ('^cat.*$') must not be anchored twice. A fix that strips every <cr>, or that rejects requests containing <cr>, changes behaviour.

O7_producer.where: cmds/server/config/types.go:196-209 (Command.Match from YAML/JSON; TrimSpace is the only normalisation) and cmds/server/config/authorizers/stringy/stringy.go:49-54 (group commands merged into the user)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The published anchoring adds ^ and $ to the raw string without wrapping it in a non-capturing group. A rule with alternation ('ls|cat') becomes '^ls|cat$', which still matches substrings at one end. A how-type variant: a correct fix has to understand regex precedence.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The fix diff itself prepends and appends anchors as plain bytes (fix.diff:132-137). This is the natural first fix, and every test that uses a single-term rule passes with it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The check for an end anchor tests only that the last byte is '$', so an escaped literal '\$' at the end is taken as an anchor.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Checking the last byte for '$' is the idiom the fix uses (fix.diff:135). A maintainer would not think about escapes.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: We could plant a second regex matcher in our copy: a regex-valued Service match in session.go:183-186 (exact equality today), or a deny-list command evaluator, without anchoring.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The README says commands match by regex and services match exactly (README.md:105,116,119). Extending services to regex for parity is a plausible change.

O9_family: authorization bypass via permissive (unanchored) regular expression (CWE-625; advisory labels CWE-1333 but the fix is anchoring, not backtracking)

O10_build.project_tests: cmds/server/config/authorizers/stringy/test/stringy_test.go (TestCommands table, mocked responses); cmds/server/test/author_test.go; root package tests via go test ./...

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Wrap each rule as '^'+rule+'$' (or call MatchString on it unchanged) in evaluate(). This forgets the trailing cmd-arg=<cr>, so legitimate requests fail, and it does not group alternations.
